member_targets: The criteria or procedure by which one establishes that externally supplied continuity information (summaries, retrieved records, user history) is adequate for a fresh generation to yield responses equivalent to those produced with retained internal state.

A method or criterion by which a system could tell apart responses produced from retained internal state versus those produced from externally supplied context at runtime, given that both can yield similar outward behavior.

Whether and by what internal means a system could tell apart retained internal state from externally supplied context at generation time — i.e., the existence and nature of a self-accessible discriminating signal or procedure, as distinct from the outward behavioral equivalence of the two cases.
The mechanism (or its absence) by which a generating system internally discriminates the provenance of available information — retained internal state versus externally supplied context at runtime.

The means or criteria by which an AI service itself tells apart information carried over as retained internal state versus information supplied at runtime through external reconstruction (summaries, retrieved records, user-provided history).

The means or criteria by which a system could internally tell apart self-retained state from externally supplied context at generation time — i.e., whether any introspective or structural marker distinguishes the two sources of prior information.

The mechanism or internal criterion by which a system could tell apart information carried over from retained internal state versus information supplied externally at runtime (summaries, retrieved records, user-provided history) during generation.
